hypothesis.statement: On a real 5-minute RR window (Fantasia f1y01), the newly-authored ecgHRVasymmetry reproduces NeuroKit2 hrv_nonlinear's heart-rate-asymmetry indices (GI/SI/PI + the deceleration/acceleration contributions C1d/C1a/C2d/C2a) BIT-FOR-BIT; and decelerations contribute MORE than accelerations to short-term variability (C1d > C1a), the established HRA signature.

analysis_plan.dataset: Fantasia Database (PhysioNet), subject f1y01 (young healthy adult), the first 5-minute RR window (392 RR intervals, integer ms at 250 Hz)

decision.threshold: descriptive: the HRA indices equal NeuroKit2 hrv_nonlinear to machine precision (max |diff| < 1e-9), AND C1d > C1a (decelerations dominate short-term variability)
